blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Tab is captured inside the open sort menu (keyboard trap)) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Keyboard users are trapped (WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap, level A; also 2.1.1 Keyboard). A keyboard user opens "Sort: Newest" with Enter, focus moves to the first item, then presses Tab to move on to the product list: the default is prevented and focus wraps to the next menu item, forever, Shift+Tab included. The only way out is to pick an option, which the menu never tells the user — and which changes the sort unless they find the already-checked one. Stop handling Tab in onKeyDown: on Tab (and Shift+Tab), close the menu and let focus move on naturally (APG menu button pattern). With Tab no longer captured, give the items tabIndex={-1} so the menu is a single tab stop navigated with the arrow keys, as the APG roving focus expects.
findings.title: Tab is captured inside the open sort menu (keyboard trap)

findings.recommendation: The handler reacts only to ArrowDown, Tab and ArrowUp; pressing Escape in the open menu does nothing, so a keyboard or screen reader user who opened it by mistake cannot dismiss it without choosing an option (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; APG menu button pattern). Handle Escape in onKeyDown: setOpen(false) and move focus back to the menu button (button.current?.focus()), without calling onChange.
findings.title: Escape does not close the sort menu

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: Screen reader users are misled (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value): the menu button always announces "collapsed", even after Enter opened the menu, so its state never matches what is on screen. Bind it to the state: aria-expanded={open}.
findings.title: aria-expanded is hard-coded to "false"

findings.recommendation: The change adds a .sort-menu class but no stylesheet; the repository has none either, so whether the focused menu item and the menu button keep a visible focus indicator (WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible) and enough contrast (1.4.11) could not be checked. Verify in the stylesheet that styles .sort-menu that no rule removes the outline without a replacement.
findings.title: Focus visibility of the menu items is not shown in the change
